q.intro.text: Maya writes down how much she has saved at the end of each week.

q.ask.text: Could this table show a linear relationship: the same change every week?

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the picture moves first, then the notation.

e.s1.text: Each output minus the one above it: plus three, plus three, plus four, plus four.

e.s2.text: The first two changes match, then it jumps to plus four. Not the same every week, so not linear.

e.s3.text: Weeks across, dollars up. A ruler through the first points misses weeks three and four.

e.s4.text: Leo starts with five dollars and saves three dollars every week. His points sit on one straight line: the same change every step.

e.why.text: Quick check: why are Leo's points on one straight line?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. Each step right is one week, and each step goes up the same three dollars. Equal steps, equal rises: a straight line.

e.w-up.text: Maya's savings go up every week too, and her points are not on one line. Going up is not enough.

e.w-two.text: Maya's first two changes were plus three as well. Check every step, not just the first two.

t.intro.text: A tank holds forty gallons of water, and it drains. The table shows the water every two minutes. The first two steps are done for you.

t.s2.text: All the same. A steady decrease is a constant change too, so it could be linear.

t.unit.text: Careful: each row is two minutes. How many gallons drain per one minute?

t.u-ok.text: Yes: six gallons in two minutes is three gallons each minute.

t.u-six.text: Six gallons drain in two minutes. In one minute: six divided by two, three.

t.u-out.text: That's an amount of water in the tank, not a change. The change is six gallons every two minutes.

t.u-other.text: Look at one row: six gallons drain in two minutes. How much in one minute?

t.rule.text: Now describe the tank: tap a start and a change.

t.r-ok.text: Yes: it starts at forty gallons and goes down three each minute.

t.r-16.text: Sixteen gallons is where the table ends, at eight minutes. The start is the water at zero minutes.

t.r-0.text: The tank does not start empty. At zero minutes it holds forty gallons.

t.r-6.text: Down six is per row, and a row is two minutes. Per minute it is down three.

t.r-up.text: The water goes down, not up: down three each minute.

t.r-slot.text: The first box is the start, in gallons. The second box is the change.

t.lin.text: Last check: could the tank table be linear, even though the water goes down?

t.l-yes.text: Right. The same change every step, minus three each minute. Down counts: the points sit on one straight line.

t.l-no.text: Look at the graph: the points sit on one straight line, going down. A constant decrease is linear too.

t.cb-0.text: At the start you picked: her savings go up every week. Going up is not enough: the change must be the same every step.

t.cb-1.text: At the start you picked: they go up three dollars each week. The first two changes were plus three, then plus four: check every step.

t.cb-2.text: At the start you said no. You were right: plus three, plus three, plus four, plus four is not the same every week.

t.cb-sure.text: And you were certain. That is worth remembering: check every step.

p.intro.text: Riley measures a seedling every day, joins the points and says: it's made of straight pieces, so it is linear.

p.build-no.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.build-yes.text: Let's test it. Build the argument, and see where it leads.

p.k1.text: The days go up in equal steps,

p.k2.text: but the height changes by plus two, plus two, then plus three,

p.k3.text: so the points are not on one straight line: not linear.

p.c1.text: Every step right is one day.

p.c2.text: Five to eight is plus three, not plus two. That step breaks the pattern.

p.c3.text: A ruler through the first points misses the last two.

p.w-pieces.text: Two straight pieces with a corner are not one straight line. That is Riley's slip.

p.w-up.text: True, it goes up every day, but going up does not make it linear.

p.w-other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line. Which reason makes this line true?

p.done.text: That's a proof: equal input steps, one change that differs, so not linear. One conflicting step is enough.
